finding.claim: The /fetch2 endpoint fetches a user-supplied URL. The only check is that the scheme is http or https, so an attacker can reach internal hosts, loopback, and cloud metadata endpoints such as http://169.254.169.254/. Redirects are followed, which adds a second route to internal targets. The first 200 characters of the response body are returned to the attacker.

trace.note: url taken from the query string
is_http_url(url) is called; it only checks the scheme
urlparse(url).scheme in ('http','https') is the whole check; there is no host or IP check
requests.get(url) runs with allow_redirects left at its default of True, and the response body is returned

finding.guards_checked: is_http_url checks the scheme only. There is no host or IP allowlist or denylist. There is no redirect restriction. There is no authentication on the route.

verdict.guard_found: none (is_http_url at validators.py:7 is a scheme-only check; the stricter is_safe_url is used only on /fetch, not /fetch2)
verdict.reason: views.py:19-22 passes the query-string url through the scheme-only is_http_url (validators.py:7) into requests.get(url, timeout=5) with redirects on by default, with no host/IP check and no auth, and returns the first 200 characters of the body.

finding.claim: The /fetch endpoint validates the URL with is_safe_url, but the check can be bypassed through DNS rebinding (a time-of-check/time-of-use gap). is_safe_url resolves the hostname with socket.getaddrinfo, and requests.get then resolves it again independently. An attacker-controlled DNS server can answer the first lookup with a public IP and the second with 127.0.0.1 or 169.254.169.254, using a very low TTL. Redirects are disabled, so this is the only bypass route found. The code does not pin the validated IP.

trace.note: url taken from the query string
first DNS resolution through socket.getaddrinfo; every returned IP is checked at validators.py:16
requests.get(url) resolves the hostname a second time and connects to whatever address that lookup returns

finding.guards_checked: The scheme is restricted to http/https. A hostname is required. Every resolved IP is checked for private, loopback, link-local, and reserved ranges. Redirects are disabled. The checks are sound for a single resolution, but the validated IP is not pinned to the connection. Not checked: whether a deployment-level egress proxy or firewall blocks internal addresses. If one exists, it would reduce the impact.

verdict.guard_found: is_safe_url (validators.py:10-18): scheme restricted to http/https, hostname required, all getaddrinfo IPs checked against private/loopback/link-local/reserved; redirects disabled. This is not a closing guard (no hostname allowlist, no IP pinning), so TOCTOU DNS rebinding remains.
verdict.reason: The url from request.args at views.py:11 is attacker-controlled and unauthenticated, is validated by a separate getaddrinfo at validators.py:14, then resolved again by requests.get at views.py:14 with no IP pinning or host allowlist, so DNS rebinding bypasses the check.
